title: Delhi HC Sends JW Marriott Aerocity Licence Dispute to Arbitration
case_name: Light Lake Enterprises Private Limited v. Aria Hotels and Consultancy Services Private Limited
card_summary: The Delhi High Court referred a commercial licence dispute over space at JW Marriott Hotel, Delhi Aerocity to arbitration, since Aria Hotels raised no objection to the arbitration clause. Light Lake Enterprises had sought Section 9 protection over a kitchen area after Aria Hotels terminated the main licence. The court appointed a retired judge as sole arbitrator and let Light Lake keep using the area meanwhile.
card_tip: A licensee holding commercial premises under an agreement with an arbitration clause should move for Section 9 interim relief without delay if the licensor restricts access pending the reference to arbitration.
verification_notes: The case name, the order number O.M.P.(I)(COMM.) 492/2026, the 4 November 2026 date, Justice Manoj Jain as the presiding judge, the appointment of retired Delhi High Court judge Justice Chander Shekhar as sole arbitrator, and the interim kitchen access are confirmed from the LiveLaw Biz report and the uploaded court order PDF, both opened in this run. The order leaves the parties' claims, objections and the arbitrability question open for the arbitrator to decide. Regional focus: Delhi Aerocity, within the firm's Delhi NCR practice base.
